# A merge that does not touch the sesam vault must auto-commit like any git merge -
# pre-merge-commit only stops the auto-commit when .sesam actually changed. Here a
# force-tracked plain file is merged; sesam stays out of the way (no finalize nag).

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Force-track a plain file (the sesam gitignore would otherwise ignore it).
exec sh -c 'printf "l1\nl2\nl3\n" > notes.txt'
exec git add -f notes.txt
exec git commit -m 'add notes'

exec git checkout -b ours
exec sh -c 'printf "OURS\nl2\nl3\n" > notes.txt'
exec git add notes.txt
exec git commit -m 'ours: first line'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sh -c 'printf "l1\nl2\nTHEIRS\n" > notes.txt'
exec git add notes.txt
exec git commit -m 'theirs: last line'

# Disjoint edits, no .sesam change -> git auto-commits the merge (exit 0), no nag.
exec git checkout ours
exec git merge theirs
! stderr 'finalize'
! exec git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD

exec sesam verify
grep 'OURS' notes.txt
grep 'THEIRS' notes.txt
